title: in/at/on (position) 3
subtitle: in hospital / at work / on a bus
summary: Learn where to use in, at and on with places like bed, work and school, with events, buildings, towns and forms of transport.

lesson.heading: in bed / at work
lesson.text: We say that somebody is **in bed / in hospital / in prison**, but **at home / at work / at school / at university / at college**.

examples.text: James isn't up yet. He's still **in bed**.
My sister is **at university**. My brother is still **at school**.

lesson.note: We say **be at home** or **be home** (with or without at), but **do something at home** (with at): I'll be home all evening. Shall we go to a restaurant or eat **at home**?

lesson.heading: at a party / at a concert
lesson.text: We say that somebody is **at** an event - a party, a meeting, a wedding, a conference, a concert.

examples.text: Were there many people **at the party** / **at the meeting** / **at the wedding**?
I saw Steve **at a conference** / **at a concert** on Saturday.

lesson.heading: in and at for buildings
lesson.text: You can often use **in** or **at** with buildings: you can eat **in** a restaurant or **at** a restaurant. We usually use **at** when we say where an event takes place, and **in** when we are thinking about the building itself.

left.label: at = the place of the event
examples: We went to a concert **at the National Concert Hall**.
There was a robbery **at the supermarket**.

right.label: in = the building itself
examples: It's always cold **in Helen's house**. The heating doesn't work well.
All the rooms **in the hotel** have air conditioning.
It was really cold **in the cinema**.

lesson.note: We say **at the station** / **at the airport**: There's no need to meet me **at the station**. We also say **at the doctor's**, **at the hairdresser's**.

left.label: in = cities, towns and villages
examples: The Louvre is a famous art museum **in Paris**.
Sam's parents live **in a village** in the south of France.

right.label: at = a point or station on a journey
examples: Does this train stop **at Oxford**? (= at Oxford station)
It was a very slow train. It stopped **at every station**.

lesson.heading: on a bus / in a car
lesson.text: We usually say **on a bus / on a train / on a plane / on a ship**, but **in a car / in a taxi**. We also say **on a bike / on a motorbike / on a horse**.

examples.text: The bus was very full. There were too many people **on it**.

lesson.text: Big things you can walk about in take on (on a train, on a plane); small things you get into take in (in a car, in a taxi).

exercises.prompt: Some people are ___ for crimes that they did not commit.
exercises.explanation: We say in prison, in hospital and in bed - without the.

exercises.prompt: Joe wasn't ___ the party. I don't know why he didn't go.
exercises.explanation: We use at for events: at the party, at the meeting, at a concert.

exercises.prompt: We walked to the restaurant, but we went home ___.
exercises.explanation: We say in a car and in a taxi (but on a bus, on a train).

exercises.prompt: I enjoyed the flight, but the food ___ was awful.
exercises.explanation: We say on a plane, on a bus, on a train and on a ship.

exercises.prompt: Match each situation with the sentence that follows it.

pairs.left: Judy is having her hair cut.

exercises.prompt: It was a very slow train. It stopped ___ every station.
exercises.explanation: A station is a point on a journey, so we say at every station.

exercises.statement: The bus was very full. There were too many people in it.
exercises.explanation: There were too many people on it. We say on a bus, not in a bus.

exercises.prompt: 'Does your sister have a job?' 'No, she's only 16. She's still ___.'
exercises.explanation: We say at school, at university and at college.

exercises.prompt: Which preposition goes with each place?
We went to see a film last night. It was really cold ___ the cinema.
exercises.explanation: Here we are thinking about the building itself, so we use in.

exercises.prompt: Vicky has gone to Japan. She's living ___.
exercises.explanation: We use in with cities, towns and villages.

exercises.statement: The meeting took place at the company's head office in Frankfurt.
exercises.explanation: Correct. At shows where the event happened; in is used with the city.
